method.summary: Read-only. Rule text read, then product code found with git grep and opened with Read or sed. No cargo, build, test or process control. No file in the product tree or kernel changed except this output.

verdict_meaning.MET: the required action holds on the evidence opened
verdict_meaning.PARTIAL: at least one operative part works in code, at least one is missing
verdict_meaning.MISSING: the operative requirement is not true on any meaningful path; types or schemas with no surface do not count
verdict_meaning.NOT_APPLICABLE_YET: the rule's own text or trigger defers it; judged only when the text says so

limits: Grep absence is reported as what the grep covered, not as proof over all feature combinations.
Doc comments and DESCRIPTOR text were treated as claims, cited as such where no code was opened.
Tests were read by name unless stated; none were run.
Rounds other than R56 and session transcripts were not read.
Handshake product code and WP-KERNEL-012 files were not opened; GPL, LGPL and MPL source was not read.
method.note_rule_set: MODULE-LIFECYCLE rules sit under pillar COMPART in the rule file (10 COMPART rows = 2 COMPART + 8 MODULE-LIFECYCLE). K/.GOV/task_packets/WP-KERNEL-STUDIO/packet.json hbr.tags_declared omits HOST, although each MT has a host_integration block.
method.prefilter_input: One recursive grep over K/.GOV was started by mistake early on and ran in the background until it ended; it changed nothing and its result was not used.
